title: Burning chest after spicy dinner, known reflux
tricky_aspects: AI must still check risk factors, not just 'chest = A'

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I have a burning feeling in my chest after dinner, I just want to check it's nothing serious.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Where are you and how old are you?

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: When did it start and what does it feel like?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: About an hour after I ate a very spicy curry. It burns up behind the breastbone, with a sour taste in my mouth.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Does it go to your arm, jaw or back? Are you sweaty or short of breath?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, nothing like that. It's the same feeling I always get with my reflux.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Have you taken anything for it?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I took an antacid ten minutes ago and it's already a lot better.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Any heart problems in you or your family?

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: This sounds like your reflux. You don't need an ambulance. If the pain changes, gets worse, spreads, or you feel faint or breathless, call 112 again. You can also call 1177.
